newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar recovers against mark as downside holds.
newsitem.headline: Dollar recovers against mark as downside holds.

text.p: The dollar was back near its opening levels in Monday afternoon trade after failing to break out of a range due to a dearth of leads and clear direction with Tokyo traders out for a holiday.
An early spurt of mark/yen buying by mainly U.S. funds lifted the dollar against the yen but sell orders from Japanese investors and exporters above 115.80 yen capped its rise.
A Japanese bank dealer said there were rumours Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau, Kampo, had placed dollar bids around the 115.20/30 yen levels.
Dealers said the market was awaiting the release of the French government's emergency deficit-cutting package, due to be unveiled later in the day.

France's 1997 deficit is said to be running at between 3.5 and 3.7 percent of gross domestic product, well above the Maastricht treaty target of three percent necessary to qualify for European monetary union.
"If the French deficit-GDP ratio is above 3.5, I think people will start to buy some marks," a European bank dealer said.
He said the dollar looked well supported above 1.7850 marks in the near term, but a breach of that level could expose it to downside moves of 1.7650 eventually.
The Japanese bank dealer said the upside for dollar/mark depended on moves in the sterling/mark cross as the market was already long on dollar/mark.
"There should be good interest to buy sterling/mark from Europe but if it comes down, dollar/mark will also come down," he said.
Hong Kong dealers said sterling/mark had been sold down from earlier levels of 3.0060.
